visual: Compact bushy fuchsia with dark green leaves and masses of small double flowers; cerise-crimson recurved sepals surround rich purple petals flushed red at the base.
water: Water regularly during active growth; keep evenly moist but never waterlogged.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged ground and very dry exposed sites.
prune: In spring, cut back dead or frost-damaged growth to healthy buds; established plants can be pruned harder to maintain a dense framework.
resilience: Hardy through much of the UK when planted deeply and mulched, but exposed growth can be damaged by severe frost and cold drying winds.
uses: Containers, cottage gardens, mixed borders, courtyard gardens and long-season summer colour.
uncertain: RHS currently lists 'Dollar Princess' as a synonym associated with the cultivar name 'Dollar Prinzessin'; 'Dollar Princess' remains the common UK trade and garden name.

visual: Low spreading evergreen shrub with glossy dark green aromatic leaves, clusters of small white spring flowers and conspicuous bright red berries on female plants.
water: Keep moderately moist, especially while establishing and during prolonged dry weather.
aspect: North, east, west or sheltered south-facing positions; best in partial or full shade.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or moderately alkaline soils are suitable.
soilWarning: Avoid very dry soil and hot exposed sun, which can cause yellowing and leaf scorch.
prune: Little pruning required; remove damaged, congested or unwanted shoots after flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten; ingestion may cause stomach upset.
resilience: Reliable hardy evergreen tolerant of shade, atmospheric pollution and some neglect once established.
uses: Shady borders, woodland-style planting, evergreen ground structure, winter berry displays and containers.
uncertain: 'Nymans' is female and requires a compatible male Skimmia nearby for reliable berry production.

visual: Compact spreading evergreen with large aromatic green leaves and dense conical clusters of strongly fragrant creamy green to greenish-yellow flowers in spring.
water: Keep moderately moist but well drained; water containers and newly planted specimens during dry spells.
aspect: North, east, west or sheltered south-facing positions; partial to full shade.
soil: Humus-rich, moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil; tolerates acid, neutral and moderately alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Hot dry sun or very poor dry soil can cause chlorosis and leaf scorch.
prune: Requires little routine pruning; remove damaged or misplaced shoots after flowering if necessary.
toxicity: Skimmia fruit is considered ornamental and should not be eaten, although this male cultivar does not itself produce berries.
resilience: Hardy, shade tolerant and relatively tolerant of atmospheric pollution and neglect once established.
uses: Shady borders, woodland gardens, fragrant spring planting, evergreen structure, containers and pollinating female Skimmias.
uncertain: 'Kew Green' is a male cultivar and therefore does not produce its own berries; it can pollinate compatible female Skimmias.

visual: Very compact evergreen rhododendron with small dark green ribbed leaves and lax clusters of vivid deep scarlet-red, slightly frilled flowers in mid-spring.
water: Keep consistently moist but well drained, using rainwater where possible in hard-water areas.
aspect: North, east or west-facing; sheltered partial shade.
soil: Leafy, humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil.
soilWarning: Requires acidic conditions; avoid alkaline or heavily limed soil and prolonged waterlogging.
prune: Minimal pruning required; remove dead or damaged growth and deadhead carefully after flowering where practical.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; keep away from grazing pets and children likely to ingest plant material.
resilience: Very cold hardy once established, though best protected from drying winds and unsuitable alkaline soil.
uses: Rock gardens, dwarf shrub borders, ericaceous beds, woodland edges and containers of ericaceous compost.

visual: Architectural palm-like evergreen with long sword-shaped burgundy to bronze leaves edged by striking reddish-pink margins; mature plants may produce fragrant white summer flowers.
water: Water regularly while establishing, then allow the soil surface to dry slightly between watering; established plants tolerate short dry periods.
aspect: South, east or west-facing; full sun to partial shade in a sheltered position.
soil: Well-drained soil of most textures and pH ranges; performs particularly well in fertile free-draining ground.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging and exposed frost pockets, especially in colder inland gardens.
prune: No routine pruning required; remove dead or damaged leaves and cut back frost-damaged stems to healthy tissue in spring.
resilience: Tolerates coastal exposure and some drought once established but is significantly less frost hardy than green Cordyline australis.
uses: Architectural planting, patio containers, gravel gardens, Mediterranean-style schemes, coastal gardens and sheltered borders.
uncertain: Charlie Boy is the trade designation associated with cultivar 'Ric01'.
